meta.title: geofare | Natural hazard and climate risk, clear enough to act on
meta.description: geofare helps municipalities, planners and asset owners make good decisions about flood risk, physical climate risk and other natural hazards.

hero.subline: We turn satellite data, GIS and hydraulic modelling into risk information you can act on. Flood risk is where we go deepest.

services.title: See what's there.
services.body: We use satellite observations, open geodata and your own records to build a clear picture of the ground as it is today.

services.title: Know what's coming.
services.body: We model how water, weather and climate can hit your area, at the level of detail the decision needs.

services.title: Decide what comes first.
services.body: We assess what is at stake and rank the measures that make a difference, so your budget goes where the risk is.

services.title: Make risk make sense.
services.body: A risk nobody understands is a risk nobody acts on. We build the maps, visuals, tools and warnings that reach the people who have to act.

mission.title: Safer communities start with risk people understand.
mission.body: geofare specialises in flood risk management, physical climate risk and other natural hazards. We use satellite data, GIS and hydraulic modelling to make risk information clear enough to act on.

founder.title: Founder-led. Hands-on.
founder.body: geofare was founded by Niklas [surname], a geologist. He thinks in landscapes, works in data, and measures his work by what people do with it. He is as much at home in satellite imagery, maps and flood models as in the room where the decision gets made.

about.quote: Too much good hazard science never reaches the people who have to decide. I started geofare to change that.

team.title: A team built around your project.
team.body: You get Niklas, not an account manager. He leads every project and brings in the right specialists from our network when a job needs more hands. You always know who is doing the work.

principles.title: Curious
principles.body: We are nerds, and we love what we do. Landscapes, water, data, models: we want to know how things really behave, and we keep digging until the picture holds. We work rigorously and from evidence, and we are happiest when a hard question turns up.

principles.title: Practical
principles.body: We believe knowledge is only worth something when someone can use it. So we prefer a useful answer in time to a perfect one too late. And because people can only act on what they understand, we make our work accessible and usable for the people who have to work with it.

principles.title: Open
principles.body: We are open by default, because we believe tools get better and communities get safer when knowledge is shared. We build on open-source technology and work in the open whenever we can.

principles.title: Impact-driven
principles.body: We do this to make a difference, not to fill shelves with reports. Our goal is that every project leaves you in a stronger position: clearer about your risk, surer of your next step, and better prepared than before.

sectors.title: Different sectors. Same question.
sectors.intro: A municipality, a grid operator and a bank have little in common, until the water rises. Then they all ask the same thing: what can hit us, and what do we do about it? Here is how we answer it for each of them.

bullets: See where flood and climate risk is highest, and what to tackle first
Get the models and maps your adaptation plan needs, and no more

bullets: Scenarios you can plan and train with
Warnings people understand and act on
Maps and dashboards that work in an operations room, not only in a report

bullets: Flood modelling for your site or plan area
Quick risk screening early, while changes are still cheap
Visuals that make the risk clear to decision-makers and the public

bullets: Flood risk per property, across your whole portfolio
Practical measures, ranked by what to do first
Plain information for residents and tenants

items.title: Government & infrastructure

bullets: Risk assessments for assets and networks, across hazards
Satellite and geodata monitoring for large areas
Tools your own teams can run

items.title: Finance & insurance

bullets: Portfolio screening for flood and climate hazards
Risk down to the single address or asset

items.title: Energy & utilities

bullets: Hazard checks for new sites before you commit
Risk assessments for plants and networks
Adaptation plans for what is already built

lab.title: Built in the open.
lab.intro: We don't only advise, we build. These are our own projects: free to use, based on open data, and made to put hazard information in front of the people who need it.

projects.title: FloodReady.dk
projects.description: A free flood risk check for every Danish home. It turns public flood data on storm surge, cloudbursts, groundwater and watercourses into one clear grade per address, from A to F.

projects.title: Vindy.dk
projects.description: Denmark's weather on one live map. Forecasts, observations, radar and satellite images from official open sources, in a map anyone can read.

projects.title: MeteoAlarm for Python
projects.description: An open-source Python package that gives developers easy access to official weather warnings across Europe. It reads the MeteoAlarm warning feeds and filters them by country, severity and type.

contact.title: Have a decision coming up?
contact.body: Tell us what you need to know. We will tell you what it takes to find out.
